$comment: Fleet client-API-key inventory (hasna/apps#1595).
Every hosted Hasna service that gates /v1/* with an API key needs exactly one
CLIENT key in Secrets Manager at hasna/oss/<app>/api-key (AWS account
hasna-internal, us-east-1). Until this file existed there was no written list,
so a service could ship, route and answer /health while nothing on any station
could call it -- which is exactly what happened to messages, and before it to
hooks, skills, emails and notes.
Defaults, so an entry only records what is exceptional:
baseUrl     https://api.hasna.com/<app>       (the Cloudflare gateway)
keySecretId hasna/oss/<app>/api-key
probePath   /v1/__fleet-key-probe__           (a path no service implements)
keyCheck    probe
probePath. The check reads the STATUS of a path no app implements: the
credential gate runs before routing, so 401/403 unkeyed plus anything else
keyed proves the key authenticates, without this file having to track another
app's routes. Services that route BEFORE they authenticate answer 404 either
way, so the default proves nothing there and those entries name a real gated
route instead. Every value below was measured against the live origin on
2026-09-04; a probePath that stops being gated is REPORTED, not silently
passed.
'source' says where the service is built. 'monorepo' entries are members of
this repository and are provisioned by their own deploy lane; 'external'
entries are built elsewhere (hasna-internal/internal-apps) and are covered by
the daily drift check only -- their keys live in the same Secrets Manager
namespace and go dead in exactly the same way.
Adding a hosted app: add it here in the same change that routes it through the
gateway. tooling/ci/tests/standard/fleet-key-provisioning.test.ts refuses an
entry that names no member and no reason to be external.

apps.notes: hooks authenticates by request SIGNATURE, not by a presented client key, so it has no API-key-gated route to probe (see hasna-fleet-key-minting). Its key must still exist; only the authentication probe is skipped, and it is listed as EXEMPT in every report.

The app hasna/apps#1595 was filed for, and the one entry that will REPORT AS FAILING until its rollout finishes. messages has no deploy lane in this repository, so nothing here can provision its key: the contracts gate added in #1758 reaches production only through an out-of-repo deploy that puts API_KEY_SIGNING_SECRET in the task environment. Sequence: (1) deploy a build carrying src/server/auth.ts with the signing secret set, (2) mint hasna/oss/messages/api-key with the in-VPC hasna-ops-mint-key-messages task, (3) confirm this check turns green. Until (1) and (2), messages-prod still answers the old static-key error and the drift report will name it every day -- which is the correct behaviour, not a bug in the check.
